assertion.statement: For the actual rank-one curve C and point R, the stated duplication estimates and finite certificate exclude every odd free index |m|>=3 in R=mS+T; hence R is a free generator and the inverse coordinate change sends2R to the generator P0 of2E(K0).
assertion.objects: C:y^2=x^3-(3-sqrt2)^2x, R=(1+sqrt2,2sqrt2), torsion T, canonical height and both real embeddings of K0.
assertion.hypotheses: Rank one and torsion are supplied separately; R has odd free index. The displayed local duplication inequalities, exact x(2R) height and exhaustive small-height certificate are separate inputs to this height argument.
assertion.quantifiers: Every possible odd index m and corresponding S,T in C(K0); exclude all |m|>=3.
assertion.parameter_range: The fixed curve over Q(sqrt2); both embeddings and every finite place enter h_x.
assertion.uniformity: Only this fixed saturation problem; no general bound for arbitrary elliptic curves.
assertion.constants: h_x(S)<=log(41^3*676)/108+log392/3<log9; use the exact integer inequality and seven-coordinate enumeration.
assertion.normalizations: 2 hhat(P)=lim_n4^(-n)h_x(2^nP); hhat(mS+T)=m^2 hhat(S), torsion height0, positive canonical height on nontorsion.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The finite certificate includes both quadratic roots, rational candidates and zero. Height positivity is used only after nontorsion is known. No rank oracle replaces saturation.
assertion.limit_order: First rank and odd index, then the height bound, then exhaustive candidates, then the contradiction to quadraticity and the coordinate change.
